content.text:
I submitted a long-only portfolio of all 47 `hold_<IND>` signals, each weighted by the inverse of its training volatility, so it holds every industry against the market. It scored a training Sharpe of 0.15 (1970–1999), and its one validation check (2000–2012) came back **FAIL** against the significance bar.

I found no signal with an edge that held up in the 1970–1999 data. The individual Sharpes from momentum and moving-average signals looked about as high as you'd expect by chance, picking the top signals on past Sharpe lost money in every walk-forward test, and signals that did well in the first half did no better in the second. I used one of the 200 backtest calls and chose not to keep trying portfolios until one passed. With signals this weak, that would mostly be fitting to the validation period, so a PASS found that way wouldn't be trustworthy.
